comment: Cellular / SIM policy for the S10+ (beyond2lte). Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-modem-diag.sh. THE HONEST POSITION: this device has a Samsung Shannon LTE modem integrated in the Exynos 9820 and there is NO upstream ModemManager plugin for it, so the default verdict is NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE / BLOCKED_FIRMWARE. This tool reports which host interfaces exist and names the first missing stage; it NEVER prints a signal, operator or registration value that was not read from a real API, and it never fakes a data connection. It never writes to any partition (modem/EFS/SEC_EFS/calibration/IMEI are read-only if referenced at all) and never touches a bootloader.

device.modem: Samsung Shannon LTE (integrated; Cat 20 LTE, no 5G)

modem_stack_truth.reason: There is no upstream ModemManager plugin for the Shannon LTE interface, and the vendor CP transport (cbd/umts character devices) is not exposed by this 4.14 vendor kernel to a mainline modem stack.
modem_stack_truth.ofono_suitability: not demonstrated for Shannon LTE; no supported AT command channel has been verified
modem_stack_truth.voLTE_posture: VoLTE/IMS is NOT implemented; calls and SMS are NOT available. See docs/volte-carrier-strategy.md.
modem_stack_truth.do_not_transplant: Pixel / Exynos 5500 / Qualcomm modem instructions must NOT be applied to this Samsung modem.

interfaces.comment: Candidate host interfaces are ENUMERATED with globs; presence of a node is evidence of a transport, NOT of a working modem.
interfaces.net_comment: A rmnet/wwan netdev is a *potential* data bearer, never a data connection. No data connection is ever reported as up unless it really is.

modemmanager.comment: The stack hop. A ModemManager plugin that knows this modem is the missing piece; its absence is the documented blocker, not a mystery.
modemmanager.suitability_note: Even with mmcli installed, without a Shannon-capable plugin ModemManager cannot probe or register this modem.

sim.comment: SIM presence is only reported from a REAL source (ModemManager's modem list, or a state file written by a real detection run). Offline/VM runs report 'unknown'. SIM PIN, IMSI and ICCID are never printed: they are redacted before they can reach a log.

supported_ui.detected_absent: the UI must be able to say SIM detected / SIM absent
supported_ui.pin_request: only where the platform supports it — on this device it is NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_DEVICE (no host modem stack)
supported_ui.carrier_identity: only from a real modem API; otherwise reported as unavailable
supported_ui.signal: only from a real modem API
supported_ui.registration: only from a real modem API
supported_ui.apn_config: an APN template exists, but it cannot be applied without a registered bearer

redaction.comment: Redaction runs on every line the tool prints from a modem source and is unit-tested offline (`redact` subcommand).

apn.comment: Templates only. Nothing here can be applied on this device today, and the tool says so instead of pretending.
apn.requires: a registered data bearer from a supported modem stack (none exists for Shannon LTE)

registration.comment: Truthful reporting contract: these fields may ONLY be filled from a live ModemManager query, and the tool never guesses.
registration.empty_means: unavailable (no supported modem stack), NOT 'no signal'

at_channel.comment: An AT channel is NOT opened by default. If the owner explicitly asks, only a read-only allowlist is permitted, every command is logged, and the output is redacted. Nothing runs at boot.
at_channel.forbidden_comment: Anything that could change radio state, unlock, write NV/EFS, or send a raw APDU is refused outright — EFS/IMEI/calibration are never touched.

protected_partitions.comment: Denylist copied from the mission invariants. No Nuxel tool reads, writes or flashes these.

diagnostics.claim_policy: never print signal/registration/operator that was not read from a real API; never claim data without a real bearer
